chunks: And remember, when We made a covenant with you whereby you agreed you will neither shed blood among you nor turn your people out of their homes, you promised, and are witness to it too.
ai.seo_question: What was the covenant God made with the Children of Israel regarding bloodshed and displacement?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as the foundational covenant (Mithaq) for the Children of Israel, establishing the prohibition of internal bloodshed and displacement as core tenets of their divine contract. The phrase 'you acknowledged while you were witnessing' underscores their conscious acceptance of these terms, making their subsequent breaches a matter of deliberate transgression rather than ignorance. This covenant is frequently linked to the broader narrative of prophetic history, where adherence to these social justice principles is seen as a prerequisite for divine favor.
